title: Ohio State Government Websites: ADA Title II PDF Accessibility | SignalFeed.dev
description: How Ohio state-government websites stand on PDF accessibility before the April 26, 2027 ADA Title II date: 44% of 356 sampled PDFs untagged, 20% scanned. Aggregate, automated signals.
h1: Ohio: Title II PDF backlog on state government websites
body:
We found 18 working state-government websites on .gov domains registered to Ohio in CISA's public .gov registry. State governments are Title II public entities, and all of them reach the ADA Title II web rule's compliance date on April 26, 2027 (28 CFR part 35, subpart H): web content, PDFs included, must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to the rule's exceptions.

Does ADA Title II apply to Ohio?

Yes. Title II is federal law and covers Ohio's state agencies and public universities, counties, cities, towns, school districts and special districts; the PDF guide covers the rule's exceptions. This is general information, not legal advice.

We measured the PDFs these sites link from their pages. This page summarizes Ohio's state-government sites as a whole. It does not name or rank individual agencies. Agencies on non-.gov addresses are not included. For cities and counties, see the city and county editions.

Ohio at a glance

  • 7 of 18 state-government sites measured with a usable sample (20 or more PDFs). Of the rest, 0 blocked our crawler and 11 could not be sampled: too few PDFs on the main site (some host documents on other systems) or a crawl that only partly finished. That is not a clean result.
  • 356 PDFs analyzed. 43.5% had no accessibility tags, higher than the national figure of 37.7%. 20.0% were scanned images with no usable text, 57.3% did not declare a document language, and 41% had no document title.
  • Spread: on 3 of the 7 measured sites more than half the sampled PDFs were untagged; on 1, fewer than 1 in 10 were. No single main issue dominated: no declared document language and missing accessibility tags led on 3 sites each.
  • 0 of 21 sampled PDFs passed the veraPDF PDF/UA-1 checks.
  • The median measured site has roughly 1,200 pages of PDFs failing at least one basic check; across the measured sites that is on the order of 46,000 pages.
  • 30% of the sampled PDFs were modified in 2024 or later. Recent documents are more likely to still be in active use, and documents used to apply for, access or participate in a service are not covered by the rule's exception for preexisting documents.

What this means for Ohio agencies

An untagged PDF gives a screen reader no headings, reading order or table structure, and a scanned one gives it nothing; both typically fail WCAG 2.1 AA and are common in reports, rules, forms and notices. Archived content and preexisting documents are exempt unless people use them to get a service, so the usual order is: fix export settings, remediate forms and service documents, then move true archives to a marked archive section.

For agendas, minutes and notices, our accessible meeting templates for small public bodies ($24, Word + PDF/UA) export tagged PDFs from Word, so new documents start out accessible.

What this is, and what it isn't

These are automated signals scaled from samples, not a conformance evaluation: a check can show a PDF fails, not that it conforms. Method: national Backlog Index page.
